newsitem.title: CHINA: China B share indices end down, A shares up.
newsitem.headline: China B share indices end down, A shares up.

text.p: China's B share indices ended slightly down on Wednesday with investors in Shanghai waiting for a better chance to cash in and foreign investors in Shenzhen selling on concerns of new clampdown measures, brokers said.

The A share markets did not lose ground because domestic investors were betting any new measures to tackle speculation would not be severe with the handover of Hong Kong less than a month away, they said.
The British colony of Hong Kong is to revert to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 and analysts say Beijing is eager to make sure nothing sullies the run-up to the handover.
The Shanghai B index edged down 0.437 points or 0.48 percent to 90.076 points on volume of 14.212 million shares worth $10.988 million, compared with $17.188 million on Tuesday.
The Shenzhen B share index fell 0.53 points or 0.33 percent to close at 158.81 on turnover of HK$74.7 million, compared with Tuesday's HK$91.4 million.

"Foreign investors were seen selling (in Shenzhen), especially some recently-listed B shares, because they are afraid Beijing will soon announce new crackdown measures," said one analyst at China Southern Securities.

Brokers said the Shenzhen B share market was still overshadowed by a front-page report in Hong Kong's South China Morning Post on Tuesday saying China's central government had plans to further depress share prices.
Shanghai brokers said some shares that institutions paid a lot of attention to have risen too much over the past few days, resulting in less follow-up speculative buying today.

"The market will linger around current levels in the short term because investors are waiting for Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle to list," another broker said, adding the company's huge capitalisation would have a major impact on the index.
Jinan Qingqi issued 230 million B shares late last week at $0.482 per share. The company has not yet given a timetable for listing but brokers said they expected it soon.
Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass was the biggest loser on poor prospects, slipping $0.040 or 8.16 percent to $0.450 on volume of 110,500 shares.
Pudong real estate Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on domestic buying, gaining $0.022 or 2.75 percent to $0.820 on volume of 1.5 million shares.

On the Shenzhen B share market, newcomer Nanjing Posts and Telecommunication slipped HK$0.07 to HK$4.18 on volume of 3.81 million shares due to selling by foreign institutions, brokers said. It was the most actively traded B share issue.

The Shanghai A index rose 24.286 points or 1.74 percent to 1,422.074 points on volume of 678.7 million shares worth 10.3 billion yuan. The SSE30 blue chip index jumped 129.478 points or 3.17 percent to 4,216.062 points.
The Shenzhen A share market rose 4.27 points or 0.91 percent to 474.17 points on turnover of 8.0 billion yuan against 9.7 billion yuan the previous session.
